To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rQdia boosts pixel-based deep reinforcement learners by equalizing their Q-value distributions.

rQdia, an auxiliary regularization loss for Q-value distribution matching, boosts DrQ and Data-Effcient Rainbow on 9/9 and 10/10 tasks respectively in the Mujoco Continuous Control Suite from images, and SAC on 18/24 Atari Arcade environments, measured in both sample-efficiency and longer-term training.

rQdia: (1) improves sample efficiency and long-term learning of pixel-based deep reinforcement learners; (2) improves the performance of DrQ, SAC, and Data-Effiicient Rainbow on 9, 10, and 18 tasks, respectively; and (3) is simple, requiring no additional architecture, hyperparameter, or training modifications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how do you make a model-free deep reinforcement learner more sample-efficient?
improving deep reinforcement learning algorithms by regularizing Q-value distributions.
the following question: Can we use image augmentation to improve deep reinforcement learning from pixels in continuous control?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rQdia improves the performance of pixel-based deep reinforcement learners, especially in the early stages of training, and that this effect is more prominent in continuous control tasks.

the addition of r-Q-DIA to the state-of-the-art pixel-based reinforcement learning algorithm (DrQ), boosts its performance across all 12 continuous control environments in the MuJoco benchmark, while also improving the performance of SAC and Data-Effcient Rainbow on Atari Arcade environments.
rQdia is a simple, yet effective auxiliary loss for pixel-based RL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rQdia improves upon the state of the art for pixel-based deep RL in both sample-efficiency and long-term learning.

rQdia is the first auxiliary loss to improve model-free continuous control in both sample efficiency (by up to 2.5x) and long-term training (up to 10x), and the first auxiliary loss in pixel-based deep RL to improve model-free discrete control in both sample and long-term efficiency (by 3x).
rQdia improves the stability of the training process, and thus the final performance, in a model-free reinforcement learning setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the auxiliary loss of rQdia is a powerful tool for regularizing Q-value distributions.
augmenting the Q-value distributions with the same augmentations as the input image is a simple, yet powerful, way of improving the performance of pixel-based reinforcement learning.
the auxiliary loss is a simple, general-purpose, and effective regularization for pixel-based deep reinforcement learners.
